1.
Project
Overview
The
HR
Employee
Records
System
is
a
serverless
web
application
for
managing
employee
records
through
a
browser-based
interface.
The
project
was
implemented
as
a
hands-on
AWS
cloud
project
using
the
supplied
HR
Employee
Records
System
guide.
The
documented
implementation
covers
a
DynamoDB
database,
IAM
permissions
and
role,
Lambda
functions
for
CRUD
operations,
API
Gateway
methods,
S3
static
website
hosting,
a
frontend,
and
example
employee
data.
Project
goal
Build
and
connect
the
cloud
components
required
for
a
simple
employee-records
application
so
that
users
can
create,
retrieve,
update,
and
delete
employee
records
through
a
web
interface.

2.
Architecture
The
application
follows
a
serverless
flow
in
which
the
frontend
is
hosted
on
S3,
requests
are
sent
to
API
Gateway,
API
Gateway
invokes
the
relevant
Lambda
function,
and
the
Lambda
function
reads
or
changes
data
in
DynamoDB.
IAM
provides
the
permissions
required
by
the
Lambda
functions.
Security
relationship:
IAM
permissions
are
attached
to
the
Lambda
execution
role
so
the
functions
can
perform
the
required
database
actions.
The
uploaded
project
evidence
documents
the
permissions/policy
and
the
role
creation.
Diagram
1
This
diagram
illustrates
the
overall
architecture

HR
Employee
Records
System.
A
user
interacts
with
the
web
application
through
a
browser.
The
frontend
is
hosted
on
Amazon
S3
and
communicates
with
Amazon
API
Gateway

HTTP
requests.
API
Gateway
routes
these
requests
to
the
appropriate
AWS
Lambda
function.
The
Lambda
functions
perform
the
required
employee-record
operation
and

with
Amazon
DynamoDB
,
where
the
employee
information
is
stored.
The
architecture
uses
a
serverless
approach,
meaning
the
application
does
not
require
a
traditional
server
to
run
the
backend
components.

Diagram
2
This
diagram
represents
the
complete
workflow
for
managing
employee
records.
The
process
begins
when
the
user
performs
an
action
through
the
web
interface.
The
frontend
sends
the
request
to
API
Gateway,
which
routes
it
to
the
appropriate
Lambda
function.
The
Lambda
function
performs
one
of
four
operations:

Create
—
adds
a
new
employee
record.

Read
—
retrieves
an
existing
employee
record.

Update
—
changes
information
in
an
existing
record.

Delete
—
removes
an
employee
record.
DynamoDB
acts
as
the
persistent
database
throughout
these
operations.
After
the
operation
is
completed,
the
result
is
returned
to
the
user
through
the
frontend.

CRUD

.
